<!-- pr-reviewer: a1a32800a85ef2e6b70356b46ab3296952b9f02e -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The safety review found no blocking defects.

- The new check uses the closest point on each segment. It includes the final segment when that segment ends inside the ring.
- If a segment fails the check, the code keeps the planned chords through the existing `push_zig` path.
- The new test checks long final and nonfinal chords in both directions. It checks that the fallback moves match the planned chord moves exactly.
- The decision file explains the choice and the alternatives. The PR meets the scope of issue #1612.

Local results after a trial merge with upstream/main at c785c14b:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Trial merge | No conflicts |
| Gate plan | Motion unit tests and two circular integration suites |
| Motion unit tests | 344 passed; 5 heavy tests ignored |
| `circular_arcs` | 5 passed |
| `circular_ramp_angle` | 2 passed |
| Clippy, motion, all targets, warnings denied | Passed |

I ran two temporary code mutations locally:

1. Remove the new segment check. The D-shaped prefix test failed with `ccw true: the 0.98 rad flat must stay chords`.
2. Change the sagitta comparison from `<=` to `>=`. The D-shaped prefix test and two valid-arc tests failed.

After I restored the source, all six ring-ramp unit tests passed. The worktree had no source changes after the tests.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes: No golden files changed. No UI files changed. No new dependency or build script changed. Tests ran locally; no GitHub runner was used. Controller hardware and the full release suite were not tested.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
